# Security & Authorization Checklist: Accounts and invitations

**Purpose**: Validate that the security and authorization requirements are complete, unambiguous and internally consistent before implementation begins
**Created**: 2026-08-30
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Coverage pass, 2026-08-31**: every item was re-read against `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/`, entry R1's and R2's artifacts, `docs/product/specifications.md` and `AGENTS.md`. Items marked **Covered** were already answered by one of those, and each names where — so a criterion satisfied by a design artifact rather than by `spec.md` is visible as such. Items marked **Resolved** were answered by amending `spec.md` in the same pass, and name the requirement that now carries them.

**Scope note**: This entry opens the last unauthenticated route in the product (FR-024) and adds the second of only two ways an account comes into being (FR-035). Both facts make the requirements below load-bearing rather than routine.

## The authorization boundary

- [x] CHK001 Is an authorization predicate specified for the address-duplication read that backs the blur check, as one is for each mutator? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009, §FR-012] — FR-012 names `inviteUser`, `resendInvite`, `revokeInvite`; FR-043 names `deactivateUser`, `reactivateUser`; FR-060 binds "every mutator this feature adds". The read that answers whether an address already has an account is none of these, yet answering it is an account-existence oracle. → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` *The one read that is not a page query* — `checkInviteAddress` is admin-only and origin-checked; `data-model.md` §3 states the same predicate.
- [x] CHK002 Is the server-side refusal predicate for `inviteUser` stated as a requirement, distinct from the inline form refusals? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-008a, §FR-009] — FR-008/FR-008a/FR-009 all describe what the *field* reports on blur. Under Principle II a blur check is a UX affordance; is there a requirement that the mutator itself refuses an address holding an account or a live invitation? → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` — `inviteUser`'s *Refuses* row carries all four refusals on the mutator itself, not on the field.
- [x] CHK003 Are the requirements clear that authentication is resolved before authorization, so an unauthenticated caller cannot reach Forbidden? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002] — FR-002 states both outcomes; is the precedence between them stated as a requirement or only implied by "MUST NOT reach it"? → **Covered**: `contracts/accounts-screen.md` *The route* — the guard order is stated as **may you be here** before **is anything here**: `requireActor()` first, then the admin check.
- [x] CHK004 Are authorization requirements consistent between the screen (FR-001, FR-002) and the mutators (FR-012, FR-043, FR-060), such that neither is the sole enforcement point? [Consistency, Spec §FR-061] → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` prelude steps 2–4 with `contracts/accounts-screen.md`'s last-admin control — the client disables, `deactivateUser` enforces.
- [x] CHK005 Is the behaviour specified for a caller whose admin role is revoked between the render and the mutator call? [Coverage, Spec §FR-062] — FR-062 covers the render and the refusal; is the in-flight case between them addressed? → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` *Why step 3 needs no cache invalidation* — `loadActor()` re-reads `user.role` per request, so the very next call is refused.

## The invitation secret

- [x] CHK006 Is the accepted token's transmission channel — a URL query parameter — assessed against its exposure surface in the requirements? [Gap, Spec §FR-024] — a secret in a query string reaches server access logs, browser history and any `Referer` header the acceptance page emits. Is that trade-off recorded as an accepted decision anywhere in the spec? → **Resolved**: `FR-024a` records the channel as an accepted decision and bounds it — single use, seven days, digest-only storage, never logged, never carried into an outgoing reference — with the trade-off restated under *Assumptions*.
- [x] CHK007 Does the spec define "invite secret" precisely enough to say whether the stored digest is also barred from read endpoints? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-014, §FR-015] — FR-015 bars "secrets"; FR-014 stores a digest. Is the digest inside or outside that bar? → **Covered**: `data-model.md` §3 "Never on this shape: `tokenDigest`" and §5 "the digest is matched, never returned"; `docs/product/specifications.md` §5 bars `invite` secrets from every read endpoint.
- [x] CHK008 Are requirements defined for a token parameter that is absent, empty, malformed, or supplied more than once? [Gap, Spec §FR-024, §FR-032] — FR-032 names three dead states, all of which presuppose a well-formed token string was received. → **Covered**: `contracts/invitations.md` *The token's shape is checked before the database is asked* — `TOKEN_SHAPE` sends an absent, empty or malformed value to **unknown** without a query.
- [x] CHK009 Is the token's entropy and encoding specified sufficiently to be verifiable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-014] — 32 random bytes and SHA-256 are stated; is the source of randomness constrained to a cryptographic one? → **Covered**: R1 `contracts/server-contracts.md` — `issueToken()` is 32 **CSPRNG** bytes, base64url, SHA-256 hex; `plan.md`'s Principle IV row names `node:crypto`.
- [x] CHK010 Are the contents of the invitation mail specified beyond the link it carries? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, §FR-017] — the message reaches an address that may not belong to the intended person; is what it discloses about the installation, the inviter or the team defined? → **Resolved**: `FR-013a` fixes what the message carries (the installation, that an administrator issued it, the link, the expiry instant) and what it MUST NOT — the issuing admin, any other account, or the size or composition of the team.
- [x] CHK011 Is a requirement stated that the superseded token becomes unresolvable on resend, rather than merely expired? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020] — FR-020 says the previous link "MUST stop working"; is the resulting state pinned to a specific one of FR-032's three? → **Covered**: `research.md` B-3 and `contracts/invitations.md` — a superseded digest matches nothing and resolves to **unknown**, which is one of `FR-032`'s three.

## The acceptance route

- [x] CHK012 Are requirements defined for an already-authenticated caller who opens an invitation link? [Gap, Spec §FR-024] — FR-024 fixes that the route is reachable *unauthenticated*, and is silent on a caller who arrives holding a live session for a different account. → **Resolved**: `FR-024b` — the route renders whatever session the caller holds, as `/signin` does under R1's `FR-060`.
- [x] CHK013 Is a request-origin or cross-site-submission requirement stated for the acceptance submission? [Gap, Spec §FR-028] — this is the only account-creating write in the product reachable by an unauthenticated caller. → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` — `assertSameOrigin` is the one prelude step `acceptInvitation` does **not** skip; R1's `FR-023` (`OT-SEC-009`) binds every mutating request.
- [x] CHK014 Are requirements defined for the disposition of any pre-existing session at the moment acceptance writes a new one? [Gap, Spec §FR-028] — FR-028 requires a session be written and the cookie set; is replacement of an existing session value specified? → **Resolved**: `FR-024b` — the cookie is overwritten with the new session, and a session already held is neither reused, extended nor deleted.
- [x] CHK015 Is FR-033's prohibition broad enough to cover indirect disclosure through the inviter's identity? [Coverage, Spec §FR-033] — FR-018 shows "who invited them" on the admin list; is the acceptance screen explicitly barred from showing it? → **Covered**: `contracts/accounts-screen.md` and `data-model.md` §5 — `/invite/accept` reads no `user` row at all, and the inviter's name lives on one.
- [x] CHK016 Are the four public routes enumerated in a way that accounts for the acceptance submission endpoint as well as the page? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-024] — FR-024 counts routes; is a mutation entry point reachable by the same unauthenticated caller counted among them or excluded by definition? → **Covered**: `research.md` C-1 and C-2 — the fourth route is a **page**; its Server Action posts to that same path, and the matcher exempts only it.
- [x] CHK017 Is the password policy requirement stated as applying at this entry point independently of the client? [Clarity, Spec §FR-027] — verify the requirement does not read as a restatement of R1's policy for a form, but as a server obligation at this route. → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` and `contracts/invitations.md` — `assertPasswordPolicy` runs on the server "whatever the form allowed".

## Enumeration and disclosure

- [x] CHK018 Is the deliberate account-existence disclosure on the closed-account sign-in message recorded as an accepted trade-off? [Assumption, Spec §FR-046] — FR-046 requires a *different* message for a closed account, which by construction distinguishes a real address from an unknown one. → **Covered**: R1 `spec.md` *Edge Cases* — the deactivated message is reachable only by someone who already proved the password, "or account existence leaks through it".
- [x] CHK019 Are the requirements consistent between FR-046's specific sign-in message and the reset flow's obligation not to vary its answer with address existence? [Consistency, Spec §FR-046] — both are sign-in-adjacent surfaces; is the difference in posture explained rather than merely stated? → **Covered**: The same R1 edge case with `FR-031`/`FR-033`: the reset answers identically and mails nothing for a closed account, because it is not gated on proving a password.
- [x] CHK020 Do FR-058's obligation to name "what failed and why" and FR-063's obligation to keep responses generic have a stated boundary between them? [Conflict, Spec §FR-058, §FR-063] — one requires specificity to the user, the other requires generality; is the dividing line defined? → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` *Refusals, and what a caller is told* — every expected refusal carries a named domain answer; anything else is generic and logged.
- [x] CHK021 Is the roster's email exposure bounded by a stated rule about who may read the `accountUser` projection? [Clarity, Spec §FR-039] — FR-039 names "this screen and a user reading their own row"; is that enforceable as written, or does it need a predicate? → **Covered**: R1 `FR-004` and `docs/product/specifications.md` §5 reserve `accountUser`; `data-model.md` §3 and §5 bind this feature to it and to `publicUser` nowhere.
- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for what a failed acceptance discloses about why it failed? [Gap, Spec §FR-034] — FR-034 refuses acceptance where the address has since acquired an account; does the refusal message reveal that an account exists at that address? → **Resolved**: `FR-034` now names that the address already has an account and points the person at sign-in, and records why that is not an enumeration leak — the caller holds a token issued for that address, as R1's deactivated message is bounded by the password.

## Session and access revocation

- [x] CHK023 Is "reads and writes stop on that account's next request" measurable as written? [Measurability, Spec §FR-045, §SC-007] — is the window between session deletion and the next request bounded, and is any cached or in-flight authorization addressed? → **Covered**: R1 `FR-020`/`FR-021` — the actor is resolved from the database on every request and a deactivated user's session resolves to no actor; R1's edge case fixes it at "the next request, not the end of a window".
- [x] CHK024 Are requirements defined for a sign-in that is in flight at the moment an account is closed? [Gap, Spec §FR-045] — FR-045 deletes existing session rows; is a session written moments later by a concurrent sign-in prevented? → **Covered**: R1 `FR-021` — a session whose user is deactivated resolves to no actor, so a row a concurrent sign-in writes moments later grants nothing.
- [x] CHK025 Are requirements stated for a closed account's ability to request or complete a password reset? [Gap, Spec §FR-046] — R1 owns the reset flow, but the interaction with closure is new here and is not addressed. → **Covered**: R1 `spec.md` *Edge Cases* and `FR-033` — a reset requested for a deactivated account answers identically and mails nothing.
- [x] CHK026 Is the acting admin's own session addressed where they close their own account? [Coverage, Spec §FR-045, Edge Cases] — the edge case notes their sessions go too; is the resulting response to the in-flight request specified? → **Covered**: `contracts/server-mutators.md` and spec *Edge Cases* — their own sessions go with the rest, so their next request redirects to `/signin`.

## Abuse and rate

- [x] CHK027 Is the absence of a throttle on invitation issuance recorded as a deliberate decision? [Gap, Spec §FR-012] — `inviteUser` is an authenticated, mail-sending entry point with no stated rate limit; the *Out of Scope* section does not name one. → **Covered**: `contracts/invitations.md` *What this contract deliberately does not contain* records the absent throttle and why; `data-model.md` §5 adds "no throttle is added".
- [x] CHK028 Are requirements defined for repeated resend of a single invitation? [Gap, Spec §FR-020] — resend mails a message on each call with no stated interval or ceiling. → **Covered**: The same two rows, with `research.md` B-3 — resend rewrites the row so exactly one link lives, and the absent rate limit is a recorded decision rather than an omission.
- [x] CHK029 Is the unbounded growth implied by indefinite retention assessed anywhere in the requirements? [Assumption, Spec §FR-031a] — retention is correctly justified; is the storage consequence acknowledged, including that it retains an email address indefinitely? → **Covered**: `research.md` B-4 and A-5 — growth is one row per accepted invitation, bounded by the people ever to hold an account on one installation.
- [x] CHK030 Are data-retention or erasure requirements stated for the addresses held in spent invitation rows? [Gap, Spec §FR-031a] — an address of someone who accepted is also on their account; an address of someone who never accepted is retained only if revoke was not used. → **Resolved**: `FR-031b` — a spent row retains no more than the account it created already holds, and no erasure path exists because no account is erased either (`OT-INV-017`).

## Traceability and coverage

- [x] CHK031 Are all security-relevant edge cases in the *Edge Cases* section backed by a numbered requirement? [Traceability, Spec Edge Cases] — several security-relevant behaviours (revoke racing acceptance, resend racing acceptance, self-closure) appear only as prose. → **Resolved**: the three unbacked behaviours now have requirements — `FR-020a` (resend racing acceptance), `FR-021a` (revoke racing acceptance, and revoke of a spent row) and `FR-045a` (self-closure).
- [x] CHK032 Does every `OT-SEC-*` and `OT-AUTHZ-*` ID assigned to this entry have at least one requirement that fully discharges it rather than merely citing it? [Traceability, checklists/requirements.md] → **Resolved**: `checklists/requirements.md` now records the sweep — each of the ten assigned IDs is discharged in full by the requirement named, with the multi-part rows broken out part by part.
- [x] CHK033 Are the security obligations this feature *inherits* from R1 distinguished from those it *adds*, so a reviewer can tell which are testable here? [Clarity, Spec Assumptions → Inherited constraints] → **Covered**: spec *Assumptions → Inherited constraints*, `plan.md`'s Summary and `research.md` F separate what is R1's from what R3 adds.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied, and name the artifact that satisfies it
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- An item covered by `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md` or a contract rather than by `spec.md` is still covered, but the spec is the artifact `/speckit-tasks` reads — several such items are worth folding back into it
